shortDescription: Finland's electricity adequacy outlook for the coming winter season is stable, provided domestic production and transmission lines operate reliably, grid operator Fingrid said on Thursday.

children: Finland's electricity adequacy outlook for the coming winter season is stable, provided domestic production and transmission lines operate reliably, grid operator Fingrid said on Thursday.
Electricity consumption is estimated to reach around 15,200 megawatts (MW) on an extremely cold and calm winter day
On such a day, domestic production is estimated to cover 12,000 MW of consumption.
The remaining 3,200 MW can be imported from Sweden and Estonia, provided that the transmission lines operate normally, the operator said.
Inflexible electricity consumption is estimated to increase by around 200 MW compared with last winter.

"Towards the end of the 2020s, the adequacy of electricity capacity is at risk of deteriorating significantly as electricity consumption increases," said Mikko Kuivaniemi, head of Fingrid's Power System Reserves unit.
He added that Finland must therefore urgently promote investments in new flexible electricity generation capacity.
